chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Abi Talhah, the seller of Sabir, and Muhammad ibn Fadl, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever withholds the right of a Muslim man while he is able to give it to him, fearing that if that right leaves his hands he will become poor, Allah is more able to make him poor than he is to make himself rich by withholding that right.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on delaying payment of a debt due to fear of poverty?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to clarify that the sin of withholding a due right (*haqq*) stems not merely from delay, but from a lack of trust in Allah’s provision (*rizq*) when one fears becoming poor. The Imam’s rhetorical question—'Was Allah not more able to impoverish you than you are to enrich yourself?'—underscores the theological principle that divine sustenance is independent of human financial status, making the act a test of *tawakkul*. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between simple delay and the ethical violation of hoarding wealth while owing others.
